claims.text: The starting material is an equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr blend containing HfH2, NbH, TaH0.5, TiH2, ZrH2, and metallic Ti/Nb powders in a polystyrene/binder matrix.
3D ink extrusion, hydrogen de-binding, and vacuum sintering at 1400°C for 18 hours with a titanium oxygen getter will improve high-temperature oxygen resistance.
The processing route causes sequential hydride decomposition in the order Ta, Nb, then Hf/Ti/Zr.
Differences in hydride formation enthalpy drive the proposed decomposition sequence.
Sequential hydride decomposition enables in-situ alloying.
Sequential hydride decomposition and the titanium getter enable oxygen scavenging.
The intervention produces controlled oxygen uptake of approximately 1.0 wt.%.
Approximately 1.0 wt.% interstitial oxygen strengthens the alloy.
Approximately 1.0 wt.% interstitial oxygen favors retention of a metastable beta-BCC phase.
Rapid water quenching from 1500°C suppresses formation of the alpha-HCP phase.
A silicide coating subsequently forms self-healing Zr/Hf oxides.
The self-healing Zr/Hf oxides provide additional oxidation resistance.
The treated alloy will be nearly fully dense.
The treated alloy will predominantly exhibit a single metastable beta-BCC phase.
The treated alloy will exhibit excellent high-temperature compression strength.
The treated alloy will have a significantly lower oxidation rate than cast or uncoated sintered HfNbTaTiZr.
The baseline oxidation-rate constant is approximately 570 mg² cm⁻⁴ h⁻¹.
Cast or uncoated sintered HfNbTaTiZr is prone to cracking, alpha-HCP embrittlement, and rapid oxidation.
At least 15 minutes of sintering is sufficient for full densification.
Oxidation performance is to be evaluated at approximately 1000°C in 1 atm oxygen for a prolonged exposure.

contradictions.description: The stated intervention does not include applying a silicide coating, but the oxidation-resistance mechanism relies on such a coating and compares the result with uncoated samples. This introduces an unlisted second intervention.
The intervention specifies sintering at 1400°C, whereas the conditions require quenching from 1500°C without specifying an intervening 1500°C heat-treatment step.
